text:
Amanda (CS): Heads-up — AcmeBank renewal meeting in 7 days. They're nervous about spikes during demos. I put together a short ops + handoff checklist for warmup, caching/batching, streaming and feedback capture. Can eng/sre + solutions confirm tactics we can hand to the customer tomorrow?

Raj (Eng): TL;DR: make it a 3-step warm path: 1) prefill common prompts to populate KV cache, 2) short-lived warm pool for demo windows, 3) fallback model with higher throughput. Example prefill curl:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefill 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -d '{"tenant_id":"acmebank-prod","prompts":["account summary","last transaction"]}'
```
Run that ~10m before demo.

Amanda (CS): Nice. For prefill volume, customer will run ~200 demo flows concurrently at peak. Does that change numbers? :thinking_face:

Raj (Eng): 200 concurrent -> use dedicated reserved slot for demo window or otherwise you'll see queueing. Set warm_pool_size to 4-6 per shard, batch_size to 8 for generation requests. Config YAML snippet:```yaml
service: redwood-runtime
warm_pool: 6
batch_target: 8
fallback_model: llm-small-quant
```
Keeps p99 latency predictable.

Mike (SRE): Add monitoring + alerts: set a short-lived alert for queue_depth > 50 and p95_latency > 800ms during demo window. Also enable request-level tracing for the tenant so we can map latency regressions to model or routing. Example alert rule:```text
- name: AcmeBank Demo Latency
  expr: p95_latency{tenant="acmebank-prod"} > 0.8
  for: 2m
  labels: {severity: "high"}
```
Make sure autoscale max is bumped for the demo window (x2) and have the fallback policy in place so traffic shifts to fallback_model if GPU pool exhausted.

Julia (Solutions): From CS side: run a 30-min smoke with the customer 24h before the renewal call: 1) confirm request shapes (long vs short sequences), 2) collect 10 sample prompts from each demo flow, 3) ask for permission to run prefill. I'll provide a one-click checklist to ops. Also, include a short feedback capture after demo: two quick questions + rating link. Suggested survey: "Was latency acceptable? (Y/N)" and "Any output issues? (free text)". We'll capture survey responses into the account ticket.

Amanda (CS): Action items: @Raj run prefill script 10m prior and verify KV hits; @Mike set alerts + increase autoscale window; @Julia supervise smoke run and send survey. I'll coordinate with AcmeBank PM to confirm times.

Raj (Eng): Confirmed. I'll run a dry-run in staging now and paste results.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: ramped-warm-pool-fix -> staging (id: d-3387). ETA 3m.

Mike (SRE): Staging dry-run logs look good — KV cache hit rate jumped from 3% -> 78% after prefill. Snippet:```text
[2026-03-22T14:05:12Z] tenant=acmebank-prod cache_hit=true latency=120ms
[2026-03-22T14:05:13Z] tenant=acmebank-prod cache_hit=true latency=110ms
```
I'll keep an eye during the demo window and escalate if p95 crosses threshold.

Julia (Solutions): I'll send the smoke checklist and survey link to the customer now. Template snippet: "Please run your demo flow and paste 3 example prompts here".

Amanda (CS): Perfect — thanks team. I'll note renewal risk as 'Medium' in the account tracker and set reminder for 24h smoke + 10m prefill before the renewal demo. Post-demo, we'll collect survey + telemetry and decide whether to recommend dedicated capacity for the renewal contract. :thumbsup:

Raj (Eng): One FYI — if we see degraded quality with the fallback_model, we have an automatic rollback policy to route a small % back to main model while we triage. I'll add that to the runbook steps.

Mike (SRE): I'll annotate the runbook with runbook checklist items for on-call: how to trigger fallback, how to scale pool manually, and where to find traces.

Amanda (CS): Great. I'll log outcome in the renewal thread after the demo and attach survey + perf summary. Closing this thread once the smoke run completes.
